documents: Published paper: Levashova et al., Geochemistry International 2022, 60(1), 1-15 (PDF)

entry.evidence: such important and informative accessory mineral as zircon remains insufficiently studied

steps.action: States the aims: explain the extreme non-formula element contents of Verkhnee Espe zircon, determine its crystallization conditions, and date it to fill the isotope-geochemical data gap.
steps.quote: This paper is aimed at unraveling the reasons of extreme contents of non-formula elements in zircon from the Verkhnee Espe granite massif

steps.action: Selects fine-grained riebeckite granite from the outer zone of the Malyi Dome, described as practically free of metasomatic transformation, as the sample.
steps.quote: We studied zircons from fine-grained riebeckite granites of the Verkhnee Espe deposit, which were sampled in the outer zone of the Malyi Dome

steps.action: Images zircon by BSE, CL and SEM-EDS and measures core trace elements by SIMS (Cameca IMS-4f); finds light cores and rims with a BSE-dark intermediate zone, and REE- and Y-rich cores.
steps.quote: The core zones of the zircon are characterized by the higher total REE content

steps.action: Infers crystallization temperatures with the Ti-in-zircon thermometer, and redox change from the Ce anomaly using a cited relation.
steps.quote: zircon was formed at ~ 700–850°С

steps.action: Describes the anomalously depleted core at point 2.1 and the BSE-dark intermediate zones, which have flat REE patterns and very high LREE, Y, Nb, Ca and Ti.
steps.quote: This zone is characterized by the high total REE content (14000–43600 ppm) mainly at the expense of LREE contribution

steps.action: Checks that the anomalous REE and Y are not an artifact of phosphate nanoinclusions in the SIMS spot, arguing from the low P relative to Y and Ca.
steps.quote: excludes a “xenotime” scheme of isomorphism and entrapment of phosphate microinclusions in the analysis field

steps.action: Describes the depleted light rims with magmatic-type REE patterns, and measures δ18O by SIMS (Cameca-1280) in 25 points.
steps.quote: Zircon rims have light gray color in the BSE image

steps.action: Determines instrumental mass fractionation on the TEMORA-2 standard and controls it with an independent 91500 standard mounted in the same sample (reported in Methods).
steps.quote: was controlled by the independent measurement of 91500 standard

steps.action: Compares the zircon δ18O values with mantle values and with published Phanerozoic granitoid zircon.
steps.quote: slightly higher than mantle values (~ 5.3‰) and in general corresponds to those of zircon from Phanerozoic granitoids

steps.action: Dates zircon by SHRIMP-II and calculates a concordant age from 7 near-concordant points with moderate U and Th, rejecting the intermediate-zone points for high common Pb.
steps.quote: The concordant age is 283 ± 3 Ma (MSWD = 0.50)

steps.action: Compares the age with published U-Pb ages of apogranites (286 ± 4 Ma) and of albitized and fenitized granites (291 ± 4 Ma) from the massif.
steps.quote: coincides within the error with an age of apogranites from this massif (U–Pb age of 286 ± 4 Ma)

steps.action: Concludes there is no significant age gap between granite crystallization and metasomatism or ore formation, and places the massif in the Lower Permian regional magmatic stage.
steps.quote: indicates the absence of a significant age gap between metasomatic process and ore formation

steps.action: Poses the hydrothermal-metasomatic origin of the intermediate zones as a rival, because their flat REE pattern is a published hallmark of such zircon.
steps.quote: The “flat” REE distribution pattern established for the intermediate zones of zircon

steps.action: Compares the zircon and host granite with the rival's other expected signs (morphology, internal structure, Ca-Ti-Sr enrichment) and reports none.
steps.quote: Evidence for metasomatic alteration are also absent in host granite.

steps.action: Brings in the authors' earlier interpretation of REE-Y-rich zircon at Yastrubets and Azov as crystallized from a residual fluid-saturated melt, as the magmatic alternative.
steps.quote: is caused by its crystallization at the late stages of the massif

steps.action: Reads element covariation diagrams (Fig. 5a-d) as a core-to-intermediate enrichment and a depleted rim, consistent with crystallization from an evolving melt.
steps.quote: Thus, the zircons demonstrate a systematic increase of trace elements from core to intermediate zones

steps.action: Compares the Verkhnee Espe trends with Yastrubets and Azov zircon (parallel trend; intermediate zones similar to the analog rims) and cites experimental mobility of HFSE in alkali- and F-rich melts.
steps.quote: define own trend (Fig. 5) parallel to the trend of zircon from riebeckite granites of the Verkhnee Espe massif

steps.action: Plots data on the Hoskin (2005) and Kirkland et al. (2009) discriminant diagrams; many points fall in or near the hydrothermal fields, and the authors set this aside.
steps.quote: Practically all data points from the core and intermediate zones of the studied zircon fall in the field of hydrothermal zircon

steps.action: Excludes an external-fluid contribution because the δ18O spread (~1‰) is within the ≤2‰ melt-fluid shift expected in high-temperature magma.
steps.quote: This indicates that the magmatic system was closed relative to the “external” fluid

steps.action: Keeps the 283 ± 3 Ma age for the massif and deposit, and a magmatic origin of the enriched intermediate zones from a trace-element-enriched melt without external fluid.
steps.quote: Obtained U–Pb zircon age of 283 ± 3 Ma for riebeckite granites is regarded as the age of the Verkhnee Espe massif

steps.action: Extends the claim, without testing it, to anomalous incompatible-element enrichment as a general feature of zircon from ore-bearing Zr-REE-Y alkaline granites and syenites.
steps.quote: We suggest that the anomalous enrichment in incompatible elements

Compositions are measured directly by SIMS; age, temperature and genesis are inferred
Explain the enrichment, find the crystallization conditions, date the massif
Hydrothermal-metasomatic zircon vs magmatic zircon from a fluid-saturated evolved melt
Partly: metasomatic morphology and signs, discriminant fields, δ18O shift
Conditions found: one granite sample from a past intrusion

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Analog massifs (Yastrubets, Azov) used as nature's repetition, qualitatively
Limited: standard controls and a phosphate-inclusion check; single sample; discriminant diagrams set aside
Age 283 ± 3 Ma kept; magmatic genesis without external fluid kept as best explanation

end.claim: The U-Pb zircon age of 283 ± 3 Ma dates the Verkhnee Espe massif and its rare earth-rare metal deposit, with no significant gap between granite crystallization and ore formation.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the SHRIMP concordia age from the 7 near-concordant core and rim points, the paper's headline 'first age' of 283 ± 3 Ma would not exist.

gates.evidence: Sampling targeted unaltered riebeckite granite to fill a data gap; no stated hypothesis directed the data acquisition (p. 2). The age could have come out discordant or in conflict with published ages (p. 10). The δ18O ≤2‰ criterion could have failed (p. 12), but contrary discriminant-diagram evidence was set aside rather than allowed to count against the magmatic interpretation (p. 12). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SHRIMP-II, Cameca IMS-4f, Cameca-1280 ion microprobes)
Scanning electron microscopy with BSE imaging, EDS and cathodoluminescence detector
CI chondrite normalization of REE (McDonough and Sun 1995)

novelty_claims.quote: First Age and Geochemical Data on Zircon from Riebeckite Granites of the Verkhnee Espe Rare Earth–Rare Metal Deposit
This study, in addition, will attempt to fill the gap in isotope-geochemical data on this massif.

limits: No review file, so the review sequence is not coded. The work rests on a single granite sample; no replicate samples or other lithologies of the massif were dated. Only 7 of 15 U-Pb points enter the age. High-U cores giving 298-319 Ma (Table 2) are not discussed (inference: possible inheritance or Pb loss left unexamined). The paper says the zircon lacks Ca, Ti and Sr enrichment as metasomatic signs (p. 10), yet reports intermediate zones with 900-8000 ppm Ca and 130-700 ppm Ti (p. 10). It also writes 'U' where Y appears to be meant in the phosphate argument (p. 10). Ti-in-zircon temperatures above 1000°C in the dark zones (Table 1) are not discussed. Discriminant diagrams placing cores and intermediate zones in hydrothermal fields are dismissed by appeal to the absence of other signs (inference: auxiliary protection without a stated test). The text reports 25 δ18O points, while Table 1 lists fewer. The Fig. 5 caption refers to 'Figures 4e and 4f'. Sub-claim statuses: magmatic genesis of the enriched intermediate zones from an evolved melt without external fluid is best_explanation; the regional Lower Permian timing is regularity-level corroboration of cited work; the generalization to ore-bearing alkaline granites and syenites (p. 13) is an untested suggestion with no status.

disagreements.target: [...] and Schaltegger 2003; Hoskin 2005; Geisler et al. 2007; Harley and Kelly 2007; Schaltegger 2007: flat REE pattern as a hallmark of hydrothermal-metasomatic zircon
disagreements.support: The authors report no metasomatic morphology or alteration in the zircon or the host granite and argue that the flat pattern here reflects an evolved magmatic melt.

disagreements.target: Discriminant diagrams of Hoskin (2005) and Kirkland et al. (2009)
disagreements.support: Although cores and intermediate zones plot in or near the hydrothermal fields, the authors override the classification using petrographic absence of alteration and δ18O.
disagreements.quote: However, as mentioned above, the signs of hydrothermal origin and metasomatic alterations in zircon were not revealed.

disagreements.target: Common view that zircon with extreme trace-element contents usually has a fluid-assisted hydrothermal-metasomatic genesis
disagreements.support: Analogy with the authors' Yastrubets and Azov zircon, together with the δ18O closure argument, supports a magmatic origin for this zircon.
disagreements.quote: usually has a fluid-assisted hydrothermal-metasomatic genesis

alternatives_considered.chosen: Concordant age from 7 near-concordant points with moderate U and Th
alternatives_considered.alternatives: All 13 to 15 analysed points, including the intermediate zones (1.1, 7.2) and discordant or high-U points
alternatives_considered.reason: High unradiogenic lead in the intermediate zones; only homogeneous domains give reliable ages

alternatives_considered.chosen: Trace elements hosted in the zircon lattice
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Xenotime-type isomorphism or entrapment of REE phosphate (micro/nano)inclusions in the analysis spot
alternatives_considered.reason: P content too low relative to Y and Ca

alternatives_considered.chosen: Magmatic zircon crystallized from an evolved, fluid-saturated melt in a closed system
alternatives_considered.reason: No metasomatic signs; δ18O variation ~1‰ is below the ≤2‰ melt-fluid shift
